answer: In a karst aquifer monitoring market, pay agents per independently surveyed sensor site, not per account. Auditors inject a randomly timed pressure ripple at a harbor outfall; upstream sensors must sign their measured response with enrolled hardware keys. Split each site's fixed reward among all agents claiming it. A thousand aliases cannot multiply that reward; earning more requires installing and auditing additional, physically distinct sensors. This limits sybils within that market, not globally.
